text: You settle down to relax. All you want is to change the channel or adjust volume. Simple control for entertainment, just needing things to work effortlessly.
Then you pick up the remote. It's no longer just a few buttons. It’s a dense, crowded landscape of tiny squares, each for an obscure function you’ve never touched.
You stare at the overwhelming grid. Is this poor design? Or are you missing something? You press a button, hoping for a miracle, but an unknown menu appears.
The system isn't about *your* needs. Manufacturers add buttons for every feature, every partner. New devices pile on more, trying to differentiate and cover all bases.
The cost of "feature creep" is clutter. Most buttons are rarely used. They create confusion, slow you down, making simple tasks feel like navigating a complex cockpit.
You still have the same remote. But now you see past the surface, understanding hidden pressures pushing design towards complexity. It's an Invisible System.
